results.claim: Last-move compression: if H is k-uniform and its classical Maker-Breaker duration τ(H)=t is finite, then θ(H)≤max{k,t−1}. More precisely, θ(H)=k when t=k, while θ(H)≤t−1 when t>k.
results.proof_sketch: Every win requires k simultaneous Maker tokens, so t≥k and θ(H)≥k. Let S be a classical strategy winning within t Maker moves. Token-game Breaker passes and relocations are handled by maintaining a virtual monotone classical history whose blue set contains the actual blue set. After each actual Breaker turn, retain all virtual blue claims and add the actual destination if it is not already virtual-blue; otherwise add any virtually free vertex. If no such vertex exists, the virtual classical board is exhausted, so the winning property of S implies that Maker has already completed an edge. Thus every vertex prescribed by S is actually free. Maker follows S with fresh tokens for her first t−1 moves. Any earlier win is final. Otherwise S prescribes on move t a vertex x completing a k-edge e. The other k−1 vertices of e are among Maker's t−1 current tokens. If t>k, exactly t−k or more current tokens lie outside e, so Maker moves one of them to x and fills e without vacating it. Hence θ(H)≤t−1. If t=k, Maker executes S with k fresh tokens, while the simultaneous-token lower bound gives θ(H)=k.

results.claim: Uniform strict half-bound: every finite-theta k-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices satisfies θ(H)≤max{k,⌊(n−1)/2⌋}. In particular, if n≥2k+1 then θ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉−1.
results.proof_sketch: Finite θ means Maker wins the unlimited-token classical game, so τ(H) is finite. A winning classical strategy must win within at most ⌈n/2⌉ Maker moves: after that many Maker turns there is no later opportunity to win on an n-vertex board. Applying last-move compression gives θ(H)≤max{k,τ(H)−1}≤max{k,⌈n/2⌉−1}=max{k,⌊(n−1)/2⌋}. If n≥2k+1, then ⌈n/2⌉−1≥k, so this maximum is ⌈n/2⌉−1.

results.claim: Exact order obstruction: a finite k-uniform hypergraph can attain θ(H)=⌈n/2⌉ only when n∈{2k−1,2k}; both orders are attainable.
results.proof_sketch: Suppose θ(H)=⌈n/2⌉. If ⌈n/2⌉>k, the strict half-bound gives θ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉−1, a contradiction. If ⌈n/2⌉<k, equality contradicts θ(H)≥k. Therefore ⌈n/2⌉=k, which holds exactly for n=2k−1 and n=2k. Conversely, at either order take the complete k-uniform hypergraph. Fewer than k tokens cannot fill an edge. Maker uses a fresh token on each of her first k turns. Before turn k, at most 2k−2 vertices are occupied, so a free vertex remains; Breaker passes or relocations only reduce that count. Maker's resulting k vertices form an edge, proving θ(H)=k=⌈n/2⌉.

final_writeup:
No fixed k≥4 admits arbitrarily large examples attaining the half-vertex bound. In fact, every finite-theta k-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices satisfies

θ(H) ≤ max{k, ⌊(n−1)/2⌋}.

Consequently, whenever n≥2k+1,

θ(H) ≤ ⌈n/2⌉−1.

Let t=τ(H), and fix a classical strategy S that wins within t Maker moves. To apply S against a token-game Breaker who may pass or relocate tokens, maintain a virtual classical history whose monotone set of blue claims contains Breaker's actual blue set. A new actual blue destination is added virtually; after a pass or a move to an already virtual-blue vertex, add any virtually free vertex. If none exists, the virtual board is exhausted and S has already won. Hence every move prescribed by S remains actually legal.

Maker now follows S using fresh tokens for her first t−1 moves. If she wins earlier, at most t−1 tokens suffice. Otherwise, immediately before move t she holds t−1 tokens, and S prescribes a free vertex x whose addition completes a k-edge e. The other k−1 vertices of e are already occupied by Maker. When t>k, at least

(t−1)−(k−1)=t−k≥1

of her tokens lies outside e. Moving such a token to x fills e without vacating any vertex of e, proving θ(H)≤t−1. If t=k, executing S with k fresh tokens gives θ(H)≤k, while filling a k-edge requires at least k simultaneous tokens; hence θ(H)=k. Thus θ(H)≤max{k,τ(H)−1}.

Finite θ implies finite τ, and the classical n-vertex game has τ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉. Substitution and the identity ⌈n/2⌉−1=⌊(n−1)/2⌋ give the stated uniform bound.

Finally, if θ(H)=⌈n/2⌉, the lower bound θ(H)≥k and the strict bound when ⌈n/2⌉>k force ⌈n/2⌉=k. Hence n is either 2k−1 or 2k. Both orders are attained by the complete k-uniform hypergraph: k tokens are necessary, and Maker can place k fresh tokens before the board is exhausted. Equality is therefore confined to two bounded orders for each fixed k, completely ruling out arbitrarily large equality examples.
